h1:
Hua Hin in 2 Days, 1 Night
Beach · Railway Station · Cicada · Vineyard
intro: Hua Hin is a seaside town just about 3 hours' drive from Bangkok, perfect for a weekend trip when you want the sea, cafes, a night market, and a bit of nature all in one go. This 2-day, 1-night plan keeps things relaxed: day one stays in town and along the beach and wraps up at Cicada Market, while day two heads out of town to a vineyard before you drive home. Every time slot is flexible, so adjust to your own pace.
chips: 🚆 Works with or without your own car

blocks.html: The nice thing about Hua Hin is that you don't have to fly or take a long leave — it's about a 3-hour drive from Bangkok. No car? There are vans and trains too. This plan centers on 4 spots that most people coming to Hua Hin don't skip: Hua Hin Beach, the old railway station, Cicada Market, and Monsoon Valley vineyard — with food stops and cafes slotted in along the way to fill out the two days.

blocks.title: Check before you go
blocks.html: Cicada Market is only open Friday, Saturday, and Sunday from 4:30 PM to 11:00 PM. To make this plan work, pick travel days where your first night lands on a market day — for example, go Saturday and return Sunday, or do Friday–Saturday.

blocks.text: How to get to Hua Hin

blocks.html: There are several ways to get from Bangkok to Hua Hin, each suited to a different kind of traveler. Here's a quick rundown before you decide. The prices below are rough ranges and can shift with the season and long weekends.

items: Your own car — the most convenient option for this plan, since day two heads out of town to the vineyard. It takes around 3 hours if traffic is light; add extra time on long weekends.
Minivan — leaves from the new Southern Bus Terminal or pickup points in town, around 180–250 THB, taking 3–4 hours. Good if you're traveling light.
Bus — more comfortable than a van, with several departures a day. It takes a bit over 4 hours and runs around 150–250 THB.

Train — you get the atmosphere and step off right at Hua Hin's lovely railway station, but it's slower than the rest, taking 4 hours or more. Fares range from a few tens to a few hundred THB depending on the class.

blocks.title: No car of your own
blocks.html: If you arrive by van or train, you can get around town by motorcycle taxi or a ride-hailing app. For day two and the vineyard, which is about 40 minutes outside town, it's worth chartering a car or booking a transfer in advance — it's better value and saves time.

blocks.text: Day 1 — Hua Hin town, the beach, and Cicada Market

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Railway Station · Hua Hin Beach · Cicada

items.activity: Arrive in Hua Hin, check in, drop your bags
items.note: If check-in isn't ready yet, leave your luggage at the hotel first and head out to explore.
Rice-porridge spots and made-to-order eateries around Chatchai Market are easy to find and cheap. Fill up before more walking.
A cream-and-red Victorian-style wooden station with the Royal Waiting Room (Phlapphla Rama VI) beside it. Entry and photos are free; skip the times when trains are pulling in for easier shots.
The beach runs about 5 km, great for a stroll and photos. Afternoons get harsh sun, so bring a hat and water.

items.activity: Rest at a seaside cafe or head back to shower
items.note: Build in some downtime before the evening market so you're not too worn out.

items.activity: Head to Cicada Market, Khao Takiab
items.note: A craft-and-art market on nearly 4 acres, open Friday–Sunday 4:30 PM–11:00 PM, with food, live music, and a stage in the garden. Go in the early evening before it gets packed.

items.activity: Dinner at Cicada and browse the handmade goods
items.note: The food zone has plenty of stalls, with prices from tens to a few hundred THB. There's parking, but on busy days you may have to circle to find a spot.
If you've still got energy, stop by the Hua Hin night market or the in-town walking street on the way.

blocks.title: An honest note on the beach and sea
blocks.html: Parts of Hua Hin Beach can get rough, especially in the monsoon season. Always check the warning flags and ask the lifeguards before going in. If it's a red flag, stick to the water's edge. Horseback riding along the beach is available too — agree on a per-ride price clearly before you get on.

blocks.text: Day 2 — Khao Takiab and a vineyard before heading home

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Khao Takiab · Monsoon Valley · back to Bangkok

items.note: If your hotel serves breakfast, eat well before you go, since today involves a fair bit of driving out of town.

items.activity: Climb Khao Takiab for the temple and the view
items.note: Wat Khao Takiab sits on a hill overlooking the beach and the wide sea, with a large Buddha image by the water. A good photo spot.

items.activity: Set off for Monsoon Valley vineyard
items.note: The vineyard is in Nong Phlap subdistrict, about 40–45 minutes from town. The final stretch is rural road, so drive carefully.

A vineyard spread over more than 550 acres, with a tram tour around the grounds, mountain-view photo spots, a restaurant, a cafe, and a wine shop. Open daily 9:00 AM–6:00 PM (Apr–Oct). Budget roughly 500–1,000 THB per person including activities and a meal.

items.activity: Lunch at the vineyard restaurant, with a wine tasting
items.note: The vineyard setting and mountain views are made for lingering. Whoever's driving should skip the alcohol and let the others taste instead.
On Sunday evenings the return trip often jams up around Phetchaburi and into Bangkok. Leaving before 3 PM is easier.

items.activity: Stop for souvenirs on the way
items.note: Popular Hua Hin souvenirs are dried squid, khanom tan (palm cake), and wine from the vineyard. Buy before you hit the highway.

blocks.title: An honest note on Khao Takiab and prices
blocks.html: Khao Takiab has lots of monkeys that like to snatch food or plastic bags — keep snacks, glasses, and valuables zipped away, and don't feed them. Room rates and tour prices in Hua Hin swing quite a bit with the season and long weekends, so during high season and holidays, book ahead and compare a few places first.

blocks.text: Tweak this plan to your style

items: With family and kids — swap day two for Vana Nava water park or Swiss Sheep Farm instead of the vineyard; the kids will have more fun.
Cafe hoppers — add time on the first afternoon for a seaside cafe near Khao Takiab, or Plearn Wan with its retro decor.
On a budget — choose a place to stay in town within walking distance of the beach, make the night market your main meal, and cut transport costs by sticking to in-town spots.
No car — for day two, pick nearby spots like Khao Takiab and seaside cafes, or charter a car for a half-day round trip to the vineyard.

faq.q: Is 2 days and 1 night enough to see Hua Hin?
faq.a: It's enough for the main spots in town plus one vineyard. Day one covers the railway station, the beach, and Cicada Market; day two climbs Khao Takiab and visits the vineyard before you head home. If you want to add a water park, a sheep farm, or Pa La-U Waterfall, bump it up to 3 days and 2 nights.

faq.q: What days is Cicada Market open?
faq.a: Cicada Market is only open Friday, Saturday, and Sunday, from 4:30 PM to 11:00 PM. To make this plan work, pick a first night that falls on a market day.

faq.q: How far is Monsoon Valley vineyard from town?
faq.a: It's in Nong Phlap subdistrict, about 40–45 minutes by car from Hua Hin town. It's open daily 9:00 AM–6:00 PM during April to October, and the budget is roughly 500–1,000 THB per person including activities and food. Without a car, it's best to charter one or book a transfer.

faq.q: Can you swim at Hua Hin Beach?
faq.a: You can on days when the wind and waves are calm, but at times — especially in the monsoon season — it gets rough, so always check the warning flags and ask the lifeguards before going in. On a red-flag day, stick to the water's edge.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit Hua Hin?
faq.a: November through February is cooler and the sea is calmer — good for walking around and swimming — but it's high season, so room and tour prices climb. The rainy season is cheaper, but keep a backup indoor plan in mind.
